<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Britton &amp; Koontz Capital Corporation was organized as a Mississippi business corporation in July 1982.&#160;&#160;Later that year, the Company became a one-bank holding company registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, when it acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Britton &amp; Koontz Bank, National Association, a national banking association headquartered in Natchez, Mississippi (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Bank is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, and stock of the Bank is the Company&#8217;s most significant asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, the Company had total consolidated assets of approximately $366 million and total consolidated stockholders&#8217; equity of approximately $39 million.&#160;&#160;Financial information about the Company, including information with respect to revenues from external customers, profit and loss and total assets for 2011 and 2010, is contained in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Dividends from the Bank are the Company&#8217;s primary source of funds to pay dividends to the Company&#8217;s shareholders.&#160;&#160;Until recently, the Bank has historically paid dividends to the Company in excess of the amount needed to satisfy dividends declared by the Company.&#160;&#160;In 2011, the Bank paid $800 thousand to the Company to partially satisfy the $1.2 million in dividends paid by the Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#INDEX">Index</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Board of Directors of the Company suspended the Company&#8217;s quarterly cash dividend for the 4<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font> quarter of 2011 and the foreseeable future in light of market conditions, the results of its operations and the results of the Bank&#8217;s most recent regulatory exam (which is discussed below).&#160;&#160;Upon (1) improvement in the credit quality of, and a reduction of the high level of credit risk in, the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio, (2) a corresponding improvement of re-investment opportunities of cash flows from both the loan portfolio and its securities investment portfolio and (3) the adoption, implementation and adherence by the Bank to a written three-year capital program, approved in advance by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (the &#8220;Comptroller&#8221;), as required by the formal written agreement dated February 21, 2012 between the Board of Directors of the Bank and the Comptroller (referred to herein as the &#8220;Formal Agreement&#8221;), which was entered into as a result of the Bank&#8217;s most recent regulatory exam, the Board of Directors of the Bank will consider the resumption of dividends, subject to compliance with such three-year capital program, which will be a condition to the resumption of dividend payments.&#160;&#160;Additionally, under the Formal Agreement, the Bank must obtain the prior written non-objection from the Assistant Deputy Comptroller before the Bank will be allowed to pay dividends to the Company.&#160;&#160;Once the Bank resumes the payment of dividends to the Company, the Board of Directors of the Company intends to resume the payment of dividends to the Company&#8217;s shareholders.&#160;&#160;For additional information, see Note M, &#8220;Regulatory Matters&#8221;, in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Effective January 1, 2007, the Company entered into a Trust Services Agreement with National Independent Trust Company, a national banking association doing business as Argent Trust Company, headquartered in Ruston, Louisiana.&#160;&#160;Argent Trust Company assumed all responsibilities associated with the Bank&#8217;s trust services, having been duly appointed successor trustee for all Bank trust accounts.&#160;&#160;Argent Trust Company performs certain fiduciary services for customers transferred from and referred by the Bank&#160;to Argent Trust Company.&#160;&#160;In return, the Bank&#160;receives a specified percentage of the fee income generated by Argent Trust Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>During the third quarter of 2009, the Company entered into a networking arrangement with Argent Financial Group, an affiliate of Argent Trust Company also based in Ruston, Louisiana, to move the Company&#8217;s brokerage business and related networking arrangements from its prior provider.&#160;&#160;Under the new networking arrangement, Argent Financial Group leases space from the Company in its Baton Rouge and Natchez offices.&#160;&#160;The Company and Argent Financial Group may refer business to their respective financial specialists, although the majority of the revenue the Company receives from this relationship is derived from lease payments by Argent Financial Group.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank provides commercial and consumer banking to customers in Adams and Warren Counties, Mississippi, and East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana, and the adjoining counties and parishes in Mississippi and Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The Bank conducts its full-service banking business from its main office and two branch offices in Natchez, Adams County, Mississippi, two branches in Vicksburg, Warren County, Mississippi, and three branch offices in Baton Rouge, East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The geographical area serviced by the Bank is economically diverse and includes public and private sector industries, such as government service, manufacturing, tourism, agriculture and oil and gas exploration.&#160;&#160;The Bank is not dependent on any one customer or group of customers in any of its activities, and it has no foreign operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The products and services offered by the Bank include personal and commercial checking accounts, money market deposit accounts, savings accounts, automated clearinghouse services, safe deposit box facilities, and brokerage services through Argent Financial Group.&#160;&#160;The Bank also offers access to automated teller machines and cash management services, including remote deposit, money transfer, direct deposit&#160;and sweep accounts.&#160;&#160;The Bank is a full-service residential and commercial mortgage lender and engages in other commercial and consumer lending activities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income from the Bank&#8217;s lending activities, including loan interest, fees and gains on sales of mortgage loans, represent the largest component of the Bank&#8217;s total operating revenue.&#160;&#160;This source accounted for 59% and 61% of the Bank&#8217;s total operating revenue during 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company expects that income from lending activities will continue in 2012 to be the leading source of income generated by the Bank&#8217;s activities.&#160;&#160;In addition to its lending activities, the Bank invests a portion of its total assets in the securities market in order to earn a higher return compared to overnight positions.&#160;&#160;Investment security purchases are monitored closely and managed on a monthly basis by an asset liability committee comprised of three non-employee directors along with the Bank&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer.&#160;&#160;Investment income represents the second largest source of revenue for the Bank.&#160;&#160;For the 2011 and 2010 fiscal years, revenue in this segment amounted to 20% and 26%, respectively, of the Bank&#8217;s total operating revenue.&#160;&#160;The bulk of the remainder of the Bank&#8217;s revenue in each of the last two years is attributable to fees related to deposit services and gains on sales of investment securities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Formal Agreement with the Comptroller of the Currency</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>On February 21, 2012, the Board of Directors of the Bank entered into the Formal Agreement with the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;The Formal Agreement is based on, and arises out of, the findings of the Comptroller during its on-site examination of the Bank as of July 6, 2011, and the Comptroller&#8217;s Report of Examination issued upon the completion of such on-site examination (the &#8220;Report of Examination&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the Agreement, the Bank is required to take the following actions within the time frames specified in the Agreement:</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">adopt, implement and adhere to a three-year written strategic plan for the Bank, approved in advance by the Comptroller, that will establish objectives for, among other things, the Bank&#8217;s overall risk profile and growth.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, the Bank must deliver to the Comptroller copies of the programs as well as periodic reports regarding various aspects of the foregoing actions.&#160;&#160;A copy of the Formal Agreement was attached as exhibit 10.1 to the Current Report on Form 8-K the Company filed with the SEC on February 21, 2012 and is incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank intends to take all actions necessary to enable it to comply with the requirements of the Formal Agreement.&#160;&#160;As of the date hereof, the Bank has established a Compliance Committee composed of (1) Robert R. Page Ogden, President &amp; CEO to oversee compliance with the Formal Agreement.&#160;&#160;By the end of March, management expects to deliver a draft of the Capital Plan, proposed changes to OREO policy and procedures, a status report on outstanding credit exceptions and a review of the annual commercial credit servicing program being implemented to the Compliance Committee for its review and comment.&#160;&#160;Although the Bank is actively addressing the requirements of the Formal Agreement, there can be no assurance that its efforts will result in satisfactory compliance since compliance is determined by the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s failure to meet the requirements of the Formal Agreement could result in regulators taking additional enforcement action against the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Individual Minimum Capital Ratios</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the Report of Examination, the Bank has also agreed to the Comptroller establishing higher individual minimum capital ratios (the &#8220;IMCRs&#8221;) for the Bank, effective as of February 21, 2012.&#160;&#160;Under the IMCRs, the Bank must maintain a Tier I capital to adjusted total assets ratio of 8% and a total risk-based capital to risk-weighted assets ratio of 12%.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, the Bank&#8217;s Tier I capital to adjusted total assets ratio was 10.91% and its total risk-based capital to risk-weighted assets ratio was 19.22%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There is significant competition among banks and bank holding companies in the Bank&#8217;s market areas and throughout Mississippi and Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The Bank competes with both national and state banks, savings and loan associations and credit unions for loans and deposits.&#160;&#160;The Bank also competes with large national banks from the principal cities in Louisiana and Mississippi for certain commercial loans.&#160;&#160;All of these numerous institutions, including the Bank, compete in the delivery of products and services on the basis of availability, quality and pricing.&#160;&#160;Many of the Bank&#8217;s competitors are better capitalized than the Bank and the Company.&#160;&#160;Most institutions track total deposits as an appropriate measure of penetration in each market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The deregulation of depository institutions as well as the increased ability of non-banking financial institutions, such as finance companies, investment companies, insurance companies, brokerage companies and several governmental agencies, to provide services previously reserved to commercial banks has further intensified competition, and we expect such competition to increase.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the Bank now competes with these non-banking financial institutions, all of which are engaged in marketing various types of loans, commercial paper, short-term obligations, investments and other services.&#160;&#160;Because non-banking financial institutions are not subject to the same regulatory restrictions as banks and bank holding companies, in many instances they operate with greater flexibility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Finally, it is unclear at this time what effects, if any, the restrictions imposed on the Bank under the Formal Agreement or the elevated capital requirements necessary to comply with the IMCRs will have on the ability of the Bank to compete with other financial institutions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Employees</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, the Company had three full-time employees, who are also&#160;employees of the Bank and compensated by the Bank.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font> The Bank had 100 full-time and 4 part-time<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>employees at December 31, 2011,&#160;and 106 full-time and 6 part-time employees at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The employees are not represented by a collective bargaining agreement.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that its relationship with its employees is good.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Supervision and Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>General</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The banking industry is extensively regulated under federal and state law.&#160;&#160;As a bank holding company, the Company is subject to regulation under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the &#8220;BHCA&#8221;), and to supervision by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the &#8220;Federal Reserve&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the BHCA, the Company may not directly or indirectly acquire the ownership or control of more than 5% of any class of voting shares or substantially all of the assets of any other company, including a bank, without the prior approval of the Federal Reserve.&#160;&#160;The BHCA further limits the activities of both the Company and the Bank to the business of banking and activities closely related or incidental to banking.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">5</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#INDEX">Index</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a national bank, the Bank is subject to supervision and regular examination by the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;The examinations are undertaken to ensure the protection of the Deposit Insurance Fund (the &#8220;DIF&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In February 2006, the Federal Deposit Insurance Reform Act of 2005 was signed into law.&#160;&#160;Among the highlights of this law was merging the Bank Insurance Fund and the Savings Association Insurance Fund into the newly-created DIF.&#160;&#160;This change was effective March 31, 2006.&#160;&#160;The FDIC maintains the DIF by assessing depository institutions an insurance premium.&#160;&#160;The amount each institution is assessed is based on the institution&#8217;s consolidated assets less its tangible capital as well as on the degree of risk the institution poses to the insurance fund.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank has recently entered into the Formal Agreement with the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;General, Formal Agreement with the Comptroller of the Currency&#8221; above for a discussion of the specific terms of the Formal Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 1991, Congress enacted the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act (&#8220;FDICIA&#8221;), which, among other things, substantially revised the depository institution regulatory and funding provisions of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.&#160;&#160;FDICIA also expanded the regulatory and enforcement powers of bank regulatory agencies.&#160;&#160;Most significantly, FDICIA mandates annual examinations of banks by their primary regulators and requires the federal banking agencies to take prompt &#8220;corrective action&#8221; whenever financial institutions do not meet minimum capital requirements.&#160;&#160;FDICIA establishes five capital tiers: &#8220;well capitalized,&#8221; &#8220;adequately capitalized,&#8221; &#8220;undercapitalized,&#8221; &#8220;significantly undercapitalized&#8221; and &#8220;critically undercapitalized.&#8221;&#160;&#160;A depository institution&#8217;s capitalization status both depends on how well its capital levels compare to various relevant capital measures and its adherence to certain other qualitative factors, as established by regulation.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, the Bank&#8217;s capital ratios exceeded those required for &#8220;well capitalized&#8221; status.&#160;&#160;As noted above, the Comptroller has established higher capital requirements on the Bank pursuant to the IMCRs, which the Bank must maintain from and after February 21, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FDICIA also prohibits a depository institution from making any capital distribution (including payment of a dividend) or paying any management fee to its holding company if the depository institution would thereafter be &#8220;undercapitalized.&#8221;&#160;&#160;See the &#8220;Restriction on Dividends&#8221; section below for dividend restrictions on the Bank under the Formal Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The banking industry is affected by the policies of the Federal Reserve.&#160;&#160;An important function of the Federal Reserve is to regulate the national supply of bank credit to moderate recessions and to curb inflation.&#160;&#160;Among the instruments of monetary policy used by the Federal Reserve to implement its objectives are open-market operations in U.S. Government securities, changes in the discount rate on bank borrowings and changes in reserve requirements on bank deposits. Changes in any of these policies can affect how the Bank operates and generates revenues.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Finally, the Company participated in the FDIC&#8217;s Transaction Account Guarantee Program, which was a part of the FDIC&#8217;s Temporary Liquidity Guarantee Program.&#160;&#160;The Transaction Account Guarantee Program expired on December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;On account of amendments to the deposit insurance provisions of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act enacted pursuant to Section 343 of the Dodd-Frank Act (as defined below), the FDIC did not have the statutory authority to extend the Transaction Account Guarantee Program.&#160;&#160;Section 343 provides for full deposit insurance for non-interest bearing deposit accounts until December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;Unlike the original Transaction Account Guarantee Program, however, interest-bearing accounts are not covered.&#160;&#160;Section 343 does not impose any separate assessment on the Bank for the insurance coverage provided thereunder.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#INDEX">Index</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interstate Banking and Branching Legislation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Act removed the restrictions on interstate branching formally contained in the Riegle-Neal Interstate Banking and Branching Efficiency Act.&#160;&#160;National and state-chartered banks are now authorized to establish de novo branches in other states if, under the laws of the state in which the branch is to be located, a bank chartered by that state would be permitted to establish the branch.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, banks will be able to enter new markets more freely.&#160;&#160;The Company from time-to-time evaluates merger and acquisition opportunities, as well as opportunities to establish additional branch offices, and it anticipates that it will continue to evaluate such opportunities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Financial Modernization</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Financial Services Modernization Act of 1999 (the &#8220;GLB Act&#8221;) affects the banking industry in three fundamental ways: (1) it repeals key provisions of the Glass-Steagall Act to permit commercial banks to affiliate with securities firms, insurance companies and other financial service providers; (2) it establishes a statutory framework pursuant to which full affiliations can occur between these entities; and (3) it provides financial services organizations with flexibility in structuring these new financial affiliations through a new entity called a &#8220;financial holding company&#8221; or through a financial subsidiary.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the GLB Act, banks are able to offer customers a wide range of financial products and services without the restraints of previous legislation. In addition, bank holding companies and other financial services providers can commence new activities or new affiliations much more readily. To take advantage of the new provisions of the GLB Act, a bank holding company must elect to become a financial holding company. Although the Company had previously elected to become a financial holding company, it has recently decertified as such as a result of its entry into the Formal Agreement.&#160;&#160;Because the Company is not engaged in any activity that requires it to be a financial holding company, the Company&#8217;s decertification as such is not expected to have an adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects, nor is it expected to result in any change in the products and services that the Bank currently offers to its customers.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to such decertification, the Company will continue to be regulated by the Federal Reserve as a bank holding company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Anti-Money Laundering</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The USA PATRIOT Act of 2001 contains the International Money Laundering Abatement and Financial Anti-Terrorism Act of 2001 (the &#8220;IMLAFA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The IMLAFA substantially broadens existing anti-money laundering legislation and the extraterritorial jurisdiction of the United States, imposes new compliance and due diligence obligations, creates new crimes and penalties, compels the production of documents located both inside and outside the United States, including those of foreign institutions that have a correspondent relationship in the United States, and clarifies the safe harbor from civil liability to customers.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Treasury Department has issued a number of regulations implementing the USA PATRIOT Act that apply certain of its requirements to financial institutions such as the Bank.&#160;&#160;The regulations impose new obligations on financial institutions to maintain appropriate policies, procedures and controls to detect, prevent and report money laundering and terrorist financing.&#160;&#160;The IMLAFA requires all &#8220;financial institutions,&#8221; as defined, to establish anti-money laundering compliance and due diligence programs.&#160;&#160;Such programs must include, among other things, adequate policies, the designation of a compliance officer, employee training programs, and an independent audit function to review and test the program.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that it has complied with the IMLAFA requirements as currently in effect.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Financial Reform Legislation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 21, 2010, President Obama signed into law the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the &#8220;Dodd-Frank Act&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Dodd-Frank Act significantly alters the current bank regulatory structure and affects the lending, investment, trading, and operating activities of financial institutions and their holding companies.&#160;&#160;The Dodd-Frank Act includes the provisions that, among other things:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Some of these provisions may have the consequence of increasing the Company&#8217;s expenses, decreasing its revenues and changing the activities in which the Company engages.&#160;&#160;The environment in which banking organizations will now operate, including legislative and regulatory changes affecting capital, liquidity, supervision, permissible activities, corporate governance and compensation, changes in fiscal policy and steps to eliminate government support for banking organizations, may have long-term effects on the profitability of banking organizations that cannot now be foreseen even at this stage of the Dodd-Frank Act&#8217;s implementation.&#160;&#160;Provisions in the legislation that revoke the Tier I capital treatment of trust preferred securities do not apply to the Company&#8217;s trust preferred securities because of the Company&#8217;s size.&#160;&#160;The specific impact of the Dodd-Frank Act on the Company&#8217;s financial performance and the markets in which it operates depends on the manner in which the relevant agencies develop and implement the required rules and the reaction of market participants to these regulatory developments.&#160;&#160;Many aspects of the Dodd-Frank Act are subject to rulemaking and will take effect over several years, making it difficult to anticipate the overall financial impact on the Company, its customers or the financial industry in general.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Further Changes in Regulatory Requirements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The United States Congress and the Mississippi legislature have periodically considered and adopted legislation that has adversely affected the profitability of the banking industry.&#160;&#160;Future legislation could further modify or eliminate geographic and other business restrictions on banks and bank holding companies and current prohibitions affecting other financial institutions, including mutual funds, securities brokerage firms, insurance companies, banks from other states and investment banking firms.&#160;&#160;In addition, the United States in general, and the financial services industry in particular, continues to recover from the economic downturn in 2008 and 2009.&#160;&#160;In response to this downturn, numerous significant legislative and regulatory changes have been proposed.&#160;&#160;The Company cannot accurately predict the ultimate outcome of such proposals or the effects of any new legislation or regulations on the business of the Company or the Bank.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Restrictions on Dividends</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is a legal entity separate and distinct from the Bank, and substantially all of the Company&#8217;s revenues result from amounts paid by the Bank, as dividends, to the Company.&#160;&#160;The payment of dividends by the Bank is, of course, dependent upon its earnings and financial condition.&#160;&#160;The Bank, however, as a national bank, is also subject to legal limitations applicable to all national banks on the amount of its earnings that it may pay as dividends.&#160;&#160;Under federal law, the directors of a national bank, after making proper deduction for all expenses and other deductions required by the Comptroller, may credit net profits to the Bank&#8217;s undivided profits account and may declare a dividend from that account of so much of the net profits as they judge expedient.&#160;&#160;The Comptroller and the Federal Reserve have each indicated that banking organizations should generally pay dividends only out of current operating earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to these general restrictions, the Formal Agreement imposes additional restrictions on the Bank&#8217;s ability to pay a dividend.&#160;&#160;As noted above, the Formal Agreement requires the Bank to adopt, with the Comptroller&#8217;s prior approval, a capital plan by May 21, 2012, which must address, among other things, the Bank&#8217;s plans for the maintenance of adequate capital, projections for growth and capital requirements and projections for the sources and timing of additional capital to satisfy the Bank&#8217;s capital needs.&#160;&#160;Management of the Bank is currently in the process of preparing the capital plan for the review and approval of both the Bank&#8217;s newly-formed Compliance Committee and the full Board of Directors and its subsequent submission to the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;Although management does not currently foresee any impediment to the Bank&#8217;s adopting the capital plan within the required timeframe, the capital plan must be approved by the Comptroller; the Bank cannot provide any assurances as to the date by which the Comptroller will approve the capital plan.&#160;&#160;The Bank may only pay a dividend if it is in compliance, and would remain in compliance after payment of the dividend, with this capital plan.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Bank must obtain prior written non-objection from the Assistant Deputy Comptroller before the Bank can declare a dividend.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Corporate Governance</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (the &#8220;Sarbanes Act&#8221;) requires publicly traded companies to adhere to several directives designed to prevent corporate misconduct.&#160;&#160;Additional duties have been placed on officers, directors, auditors and attorneys of public companies.&#160;&#160;The Sarbanes Act requires certifications regarding financial statement accuracy and internal control adequacy by the chief executive officer and chief financial officer of the Company in periodic and annual reports filed with the SEC.&#160;&#160;The Sarbanes Act also accelerates insider reporting obligations under Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, restricts certain executive officer and director transactions, imposes new obligations on corporate audit committees and provides for enhanced review by the SEC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Item 1A.&#160;&#160;Risk <a name="I1A">Factors.</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On March 12, 2012, there were 457 shareholders of record of the Company&#8217;s common stock, and the price of the Company&#8217;s common stock was $8.55.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Historically, the Company has declared dividends on a quarterly basis. Funds for the payment of cash dividends are obtained from dividends received by the Company from the Bank.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the declaration and payment of cash dividends by the Company depends upon the Bank&#8217;s earnings, financial condition, general economic conditions, compliance with regulatory requirements and other factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The Board of Directors of the Company suspended the Company&#8217;s quarterly cash dividend for the 4th quarter of 2011 and the foreseeable future in light of market conditions, the results of its operations and the results of the Bank&#8217;s most recent regulatory exam (which is discussed below).&#160;&#160;Upon improvement in the credit quality of and a reduction of the high level of credit risk in the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio, a corresponding improvement of re-investment opportunities of cash flows from both the loan portfolio and its securities investment portfolio and the adoption, implementation and adherence by the Bank to a written three-year capital program, approved in advance by the Comptroller, the Board of Directors of the Bank will consider the resumption of dividends, subject to compliance with such three-year capital program, which will be a condition to the resumption of dividend payments.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Bank must obtain the prior written non-objection from the Assistant Deputy Comptroller before the Bank will be allowed to pay dividends to the Company.&#160;&#160;Once the Bank resumes the payment of dividends to the Company, the Board of Directors of the Company intends to resume the payment of dividends to the Company&#8217;s shareholders.&#160;&#160;There are also restrictions on the Bank&#8217;s ability to transfer funds to the Company in the form of cash dividends under federal and state law and regulations pursuant to the Formal Agreement.&#160;&#160;See Note M, &#8220;Regulatory Matters&#8221;, in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, for a discussion of these restrictions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">No disclosure is required hereunder as the Company is a &#8220;smaller reporting company,&#8221; as defined in Item 10(f) of Regulation S-K.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Item 7.&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of <a name="I7">Operations.</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This discussion presents a review of the major factors that have affected the financial condition, changes in financial condition and results of operations of the Company and its subsidiaries, principally the Bank, as of and for the years ended December 31, 2011 and December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Summary</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2011, the Company reported net income of $394 thousand, or $.18 per basic and diluted share, compared to net income of $1.9 million, or $.90 per basic and diluted share, reported at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Returns on average assets and equity for the year ended December 31, 2011, were .11% and 1.00%, respectively, compared to .51% and 4.76%, respectively, for same period in 2010.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Prior to giving effect to the tax benefit, returns on average assets and equity for the year ended December 31, 2011, were (.02%) and (.21%), respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2011, and predominantly in the last half of the year, the Company&#8217;s overall asset quality continued to deteriorate due mainly to the ongoing effects of the economic downturn affecting the United States as a whole and the local markets in which the Company operates, particularly the Baton Rouge, Louisiana, market, coupled with our underwriting practices in the Baton Rouge, market.&#160;&#160;In addition to the decline in loan demand, the Company transferred $6.8 million in loans to non-accrual during the year, other real estate increased $398 thousand to $3.7 million as net charge-offs decreased by only $309 thousand.&#160;&#160;The Company increased the allowance for loan and lease losses by $1.9 million to $4.3 million in an effort to provide for the increased level of non-performing assets in 2011.&#160;&#160;The Company continues to attempt to resolve these issues quickly through foreclosure and sale of collateral.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the Formal Agreement and the Company&#8217;s existing policies, management is in the process of reviewing areas of credit and risk analysis to ensure that its credit administration and loan underwriting processes are improved and focused on the creditworthiness of new and existing borrowers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Formal Agreement and IMCRs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>As described in detail under the heading &#8220;General&#8212;Formal Agreement&#8221; and &#8220;&#8212;Individual Minimum Capital Ratios&#8221; in Item 1, Business, above, as a result of the Comptroller&#8217;s Report of Examination of the Bank as of July 6, 2011, on February 21, 2012, the Board of Directors of the Bank entered into the Formal Agreement with the Comptroller.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Comptroller established higher individual minimum capital ratios (the &#8220;IMCRs&#8221;) for the Bank, effective as of February 21, 2012.&#160;&#160;Please refer to the above-referenced section of Item 1, Business, for more specific information regarding the Formal Agreement and the IMCRs, including the status of the Bank&#8217;s efforts to implement the provisions of the Formal Agreement.&#160;&#160;It is unclear at this time what effects, if any, the restrictions imposed on the Bank under the Formal Agreement or the elevated capital requirements necessary to comply with the IMCRs will have on the Company&#8217;s and the Bank&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financial Condition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Total assets decreased $9.3 million to $366.1 million at December 31, 2011, as compared to total assets of $375.4 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The change is due primarily to decreases in total investment securities of $19.9 million, a drop in net loans of $31.5 million, an increase in cash and due from banks of $42.8 million and an increase in other real estate of $398 thousand.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The decrease in investment securities is due to a lack of attractive re-investment opportunities during the year; instead, liquidity from the securities portfolio was used to repay debt.&#160;&#160;The decline in loans is mainly due to the continued depressed economic conditions affecting the United States and the Company&#8217;s local markets, exacerbated by loan underwriting and monitoring practices in the Company&#8217;s Baton Rouge market (which practices are being revised in connection with the Formal Agreement).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Average Earning Assets.</font>&#160;&#160;Interest income from earning assets represents the Company&#8217;s main source of revenue.&#160;&#160;Average earning assets for the year ended December 31, 2011, totaled $355.6 million, a $1.5 million decline from the $357.1 million at December 31, 2010.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Income from earning assets decreased over $3 million which is the result of the shift mentioned above from longer term, higher yielding assets to shorter term, lower yielding assets.&#160;&#160;In 2011, loans comprised 56% of average earning assets compared to 62% in 2010, while investments decreased to 35% of average earning assets in 2011 from 38% in 2010.&#160;&#160;The balance, which was held in short-term funds, increased $30.0 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investment Securities.&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>The Company&#8217;s securities at December 31, 2011, consist primarily of mortgage-backed securities, municipal investments and equity securities.&#160;&#160;Securities deemed to be held-to-maturity (&#8220;HTM&#8221;) are accounted for by the amortized cost method and represented approximately 22% of total securities at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Securities designated as available-for-sale (&#8220;AFS&#8221;) are accounted for at fair value with valuation adjustments recorded in the equity section of the Company&#8217;s balance sheet through other comprehensive income/(loss).&#160;&#160;AFS securities comprised approximately 77% of total investment securities at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Equity securities accounted for the remaining 1%.&#160;&#160;There were no securities categorized as trading at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The Company classifies its security purchases at acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The $19.9 million decrease in investment securities was a result of the sustained lower interest rate environment during 2011, which made profitable reinvestment of cash flows back into the market difficult.&#160;&#160;Instead, cash flows were primarily used to repay short-term debt and build cash.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loans.&#160;&#160;</font>Loans represent the Company&#8217;s largest source of revenue.&#160;&#160;Total loans at December 31, 2011, of $187.1 million represent a decrease of $29.6 million compared to $216.6 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Most of the decrease, approximately $20 million, came from the Company&#8217;s Baton Rouge, Louisiana, market.&#160;&#160;In 2012, the Company expects minimal loan growth in all of its markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although the Company generally sells all of its 1-4 family residential loans, this portfolio has declined or remained relatively the same over the last few years.&#160;&#160;From time-to-time, the Company, as part of its asset liability analysis, will periodically hold short-term residential loans in an effort to lessen the decline of its total loan portfolio and thus generate additional interest income.&#160;&#160;Total residential loans originated and sold during 2011 were $42.4 million, a slight decrease from $46.4 million in 2010.&#160;&#160;The decrease in mortgage originations is due primarily to the economy and the loss of two mortgage originators early in 2011 that were not replaced until the 4<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font> quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;Loans held for sale decreased $3.2 million to $2.9 million at December 31, 2011, compared to $6.1 million at December 31, 2010, as the speed in investor payoffs accelerated.&#160;&#160;Management expects total originations and fee income generated in 2012 to equal or surpass the results in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asset Quality</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management continually monitors the&#160;diversification of the loan portfolio and assesses loan quality.&#160;&#160;When the assessment of an individual loan relationship indicates that the borrower has a defined weakness in the ability to repay and the collection of all outstanding principal and/or interest is in doubt, the debt is placed on non-accrual.&#160; By placing loans on non-accrual the Company recognizes a problem credit, discontinues the accrual of interest that is likely uncollectible (unless the net realizable value of any collateral securing the loan is sufficient to cover its principal balance and accrued interest), and adjusts the carried loan balance to reflect the collection amount expected.&#160;&#160;In addition, all previously accrued and uncollected interest for the year is reversed against interest income.&#160;&#160;A non-accrual loan may be restored to accrual status when it is no longer delinquent and management no longer doubts the collectability of interest and principal.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Comptroller&#8217;s Report of Examination highlighted certain deficiencies in the Company&#8217;s policies and procedures for monitoring the loan portfolio and assessing asset quality.&#160;&#160;Among other things, the Comptroller found that: (1) cash flow analysis to determine a borrower&#8217;s ability to repay was not performed consistently, (2) the Company did not perform necessary post-funding analysis on large or complex credits, and (3) credit and collateral exceptions were too high, with insufficient processes to reduce these exceptions.&#160;&#160;In the Formal Agreement, the Bank committed to addressing these and other deficiencies noted in the Report of Examination.&#160;&#160;In management&#8217;s opinion, the Bank has made measurable progress in rectifying the issues noted in the Report of Examination, and management will continue to work with the Comptroller to meet its obligations under the Formal Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Several key measures are used to evaluate and monitor the Company&#8217;s asset quality.&#160;&#160;These measures include the levels and percentages of total nonperforming assets, loan delinquencies, non-accrual loans, foreclosed assets and charge-offs.&#160;&#160;The economic downturn affecting the United States, the related decline of economic activity in the Company&#8217;s markets and our underwriting practices in its Baton Rouge, Louisiana, market affected nonperforming assets in 2011.&#160;&#160;Nonperforming assets, consisting of non-accrual loans, loans past due 90 days or more and other real estate owned, increased to $12.7 million at December 31, 2011, compared to $11.3 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;As discussed below under &#8220;Allowance for Loan Losses,&#8221; one larger loan secured by multi-family residential property was a major contributor to the increased level of nonperforming assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Even as intensified efforts on problem credits during 2011 have increased, charge-offs have declined since the previous year-end.&#160;&#160;Management expects the economic environment in the Company&#8217;s three markets to remain sluggish in 2012, as the timing of recovery in the national and particularly the local markets is unknown.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the enhanced loan monitoring procedures being implemented in connection with the Formal Agreement will bolster the Company&#8217;s ability to anticipate potential problems in the loan portfolio and take appropriate action.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, loan classification is an on-going, dynamic process, and the migration of loans into an impaired status cannot be predicted with total accuracy, especially in light of the current economic climate in the United States.</font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#INDEX">Index</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is available to absorb&#160;probable credit losses inherent in the entire loan portfolio. The appropriate level of the allowance is based on an ongoing analysis of the loan portfolio and represents an amount that management deems adequate to provide for inherent losses.&#160;&#160;The balance of the loans determined to be impaired under ASC 310, &#8220;Receivables,&#8221; and the related allowance is included in management&#8217;s estimation and analysis of the allowance for loan losses. The determination of the appropriate level of the allowance is sensitive to a variety of internal factors, primarily historical loss ratios and assigned risk ratings, and external factors, primarily the economic environment. Additionally, the estimate of the allowance required to absorb credit losses in the entire portfolio may change due to shifts in the mix and level of loan balances outstanding and in prevailing economic conditions, as evidenced by changes in real estate demand and values, interest rates, unemployment rates and energy costs. While no one factor is dominant, each could cause actual loan losses to differ materially from originally estimated amounts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For portfolio balances of consumer, consumer mortgage and certain other similar loan types, allowance factors are determined based on historical loss ratios by portfolio and may be adjusted by other qualitative criteria. For larger commercial and commercial real estate secured loans, risk-rating grades are assigned by lending, credit administration or loan review personnel, based on an analysis of the financial and collateral strength and other credit attributes underlying each loan. The allowance factors are established based on historical loss ratios experienced by the Company for these loan types, as well as the credit quality criteria underlying each grade, adjusted for trends and expectations about losses inherent in our existing portfolios. In making these adjustments to the allowance factors, management takes into consideration factors which it believes are causing, or likely to cause, losses within our loan portfolio but which may not be fully reflected in our historical loss ratios.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal and interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement. Impairment is measured on a loan-by-loan basis for problem loans by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate, the loan&#8217;s observable market price or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&#160;&#160;For real estate collateral, the fair market value of the collateral is based upon a recent appraisal by a qualified and licensed appraiser of the underlying collateral.&#160;&#160;The process by which management determines the appropriate level of the allowance and the corresponding provision for probable credit losses involves considerable judgment; therefore, no assurance can be given that future losses will not vary from current estimates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company allowance for loan losses increased $1.9 million to $4.3 million at December 31, 2011, compared to $2.4 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The higher amount in 2011 was primarily due to increased problem assets (including those identified in connection with the Comptroller&#8217;s Report of Examination) including a $4.2 million multi-family loan that was placed on non-accrual in the 3rd quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, management believes the allowance for loan losses of $4.3&#160;million is adequate, under prevailing economic conditions, to absorb probable losses on existing loans.&#160;&#160;The allowance includes an allocation of approximately $2.4 million on total impaired loans of $8.8 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the fourth quarter of 2009, the Company hired a certified real estate appraiser to oversee the internal appraisal review process.&#160;&#160;Also, effective January 1, 2010, the Company adopted a new policy that governs the ordering, scope, independence and review of real estate appraisals used in the lending function which is designed to reduce the Company&#8217;s risks in real estate secured loans.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Comptroller&#8217;s Report of Examination noted that the appraisal policy did not state clearly enough when new appraisals were required and did not provide enough detail regarding requirements for appraisals.&#160;&#160;As required under the Formal Agreement, management is in the process of updating its appraisal policy and procedures to contain the required details and is obtaining&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">supporting documentation for appraisals and ordering updated appraisals as necessary.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In foreclosure situations, the Bank obtains independent appraisals.&#160;&#160;The Bank transfers most of its foreclosed properties to Other Real Estate Owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) at the fair value less sales commission and related marketing costs.&#160;&#160;Any remaining balance of the impaired loan is charged to the allowance for loan losses.&#160;&#160;Although there have been instances in which the Bank has recorded foreclosed properties at less than fair value net of costs to sell, the Bank has determined that, as of December 31, 2011, such additional discounts to foreclosed properties&#8217; value totaled less than $50 thousand in the aggregate.&#160;&#160;However, as required by the Formal Agreement, the Bank will update its OREO policy to address appropriate accounting and operating procedures to adhere to the specific rules governing the carrying value of OREO.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When the Company determines that a loan is nonperforming or impaired through its ongoing loan review process or, less frequently, receives notice of the occurrence of events impacting the collectability of a loan, its emphasis promptly shifts to the evaluation of the loan collateral.&#160;&#160;The evaluation of such collateral involves input from several parties within the bank:&#160;&#160;loan review, credit administration, the in-house appraisal review officer, and the relevant lending officer.&#160;&#160;Following such input, the Company&#8217;s chief credit policy officer makes the final determination regarding whether to order new appraisals of the real estate collateral or an update to an existing appraisal.&#160;&#160;Write-downs and charge-offs resulting from the credit review and collection processes are reviewed monthly by the independent members of the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;There is typically no significant timing difference in ordering appraisals and the recognition of provision or related charge-off.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The increase in deposits in 2011 was primarily due to increases in non-interest bearing deposits and NOW accounts, along with smaller increases in other non-maturity deposits.&#160;&#160;These deposit increases were offset by declines in certificate of deposits because as predicted depositors held their deposits in short-term instruments in this period of lower interest rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company maintains wholesale deposit funding sources to provide additional liquidity if necessary.&#160;&#160;The Company belongs to a network that allows access to national deposits and has the ability to gather these deposits as needed.&#160;&#160;It also is a member of the Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service (&#8220;CDARS&#8221;), a deposit placement network.&#160;&#160;Deposits in the CDARS program are federally insured and are considered brokered.&#160;&#160;Because of the brokered classification, the Company considers these deposits as non-core; however, they have remained relatively stable over the past several years ending December 31, 2011, at $17.3 million compared to $11.8 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The increase is due to a new CDARS instrument called Insured Cash Sweeps.&#160;&#160;This allows the customer to deposit funds that have the same FDIC protection as the term deposits but with the capability to withdraw funds with similar characteristics as a money market deposit.</font></div>
